Query SQL Server as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__sql_server.R
oauth_db_sql_server.Rd

Use this for SQL Server configured to accept Microsoft Entra tokens. It takes the same connection arguments as oauth_db_azure_sql().

Usage

oauth_db_sql_server(
  authorization,
  server,
  database,
  ...,
  target = "sql",
  required_scopes = character(),
  driver = "ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server",
  port = 1433L,
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

server

Database hostname.

database

Database name.

...

Named odbc connection options, such as timeout. The helper sets authentication and verified TLS.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

driver

Installed ODBC driver name.

port

Database port.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

A reactive function returning an odbc DBI connection.

Details

Create the helper inside server() and call it inside a render or reactive expression before querying with DBI or dbplyr.

See also

oauth_db_azure_sql(), oauth_db_microsoft_client(). vignette("azure-sql", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Other database connections: oauth_db_azure_postgres(), oauth_db_azure_sql(), oauth_db_databricks(), oauth_db_duckdb(), oauth_db_fabric_sql(), oauth_db_hana(), oauth_db_oracle(), oauth_db_postgres(), oauth_db_redshift(), oauth_db_snowflake(), oauth_db_starrocks(), oauth_db_trino()
